title: Per-request circuit policy and deferred retry saga for hosted API stability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a per-request circuit policy combined with a deferred-retry saga to reduce 5xx amplification during tenant surges and customer escalations. The solution should prevent global tenant-wide quarantine, provide fine-grained automatic fast-fail for repeated failing request signatures, and allow safe deferred retries coordinated by a lightweight durable store to avoid synchronized retry storms.
acceptance_criteria: Per-request circuit metadata propagated end-to-end (edge -> proxy -> runtime) for >95% of requests in staging
Deferred retry saga persists retry intent and backoff metadata in the durable store and is replayable without client-side retries
Observed production-like tenant surge test shows 60% reduction in backend 5xx amplification vs current baseline
Dashboards for per-request circuit hits, deferred-saga queue depth, and downstream success-after-retry available in Console with alerting thresholds
Graceful rollback via feature flag or rollout policy with no config migration required
notes: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after two escalations where client retry storms coincided with KV cache eviction and upstream kernel saturation.
2026-03-11: Spike reproduction plan defined with synthetic tenant burst harness in staging; added Canary group for 5% of traffic.

2026-03-12: Design review with Runtime and Edge teams: agreed on lightweight signature (method+model+prefix-hash+client-id) and TTL=120s by default; trade-off: signature collision risk vs. memory overhead discussed.
2026-03-12: Trade-off decision: use in-memory LRU at edge with optional fallback to Redis for long tail; initial rollout uses in-memory only to avoid network dependencies.
2026-03-13: Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1482 — implements per-request circuit header propagation and local circuit evaluation.
2026-03-13: Security review flagged that deferred saga will touch audit logs; SRE asked to ensure KMS key usage for durable store encryption for production rollout.

2026-03-14: Observability plan: add three new metrics - request_signature_circuit_open_total, deferred_saga_enqueue_total, deferred_saga_success_after_replay_total. Dashboard draft at https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/ENG-799321

2026-03-14: QA discovered an edge-case where streaming requests without Content-Length could create poorly formed signatures; mitigation: normalize by using first-512-b prefix and stable model name string.

2026-03-14: Scoped canary rollout plan: enable on 5% edge nodes, monitor 5xx, tail latency, and dashboard alarms for 30m, then 25%, 50%, 100% if green. Rollback criteria: >10% increase in 5xx or >25ms p95 latency increase sustained for 10m.
Links: Confluence design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-799321, Incident notes https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/hosted-escalation-2026-03
implementation_steps: Edge: implement signature generation and in-memory LRU circuit evaluator; emit header X-RW-Req-Sig and X-RW-Circuit-Status
Proxy: read circuit header and short-circuit requests where signature is open; return stable error code 429 or 499 to indicate fast-fail to clients
Runtime: accept circuit status header; for deferred retries, expose an endpoint to enqueue retry intent into durable store with backoff metadata
Durable store: lightweight Redis list + capped retention for saga intents; support idempotent replay with idempotency key = signature+nonce
Controller: background replay worker with jittered exponential backoff and rate limit towards runtime capacity signals
Observability: instrument metrics, traces, and add SLO-comparison alerts and a Console dashboard tile
Runbook: update incident runbook with steps to toggle feature flags, inspect saga queue, and force-replay or purge intents
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signature collisions causing unrelated requests to be fast-failed. Mitigation: use 64-bit prefix-hash + model+client salt; monitor collision rate metric and raise TTL if high.
Risk: Durable store becomes new amplification point. Mitigation: cap enqueue rate per-tenant, evict oldest intents beyond retention window, and use backpressure signals from controller.

Risk: Increased tail latency when replaying deferred retries. Mitigation: controller reads runtime capacity signals and replays only into safe windows; preferentially route replays to low-utilization backends.
Risk: Observability blind spots. Mitigation: sample 1% of full request payloads for offline analysis and correlate with PRs and audit logs.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (staging): full integration tests + synthetic tenant surge runs (3x baseline) — target completion 2026-03-16
Stage 2 (canary): enable on 5% of edge nodes for 2h, monitor dashboards and log sampling; abort window 30m — target 2026-03-18
Stage 3 (ramped canary): 25% -> 50% over 24h if no alerts triggered
Stage 4: full production enable with continuous monitoring and 12h post-rollout review
rollback_criteria: Sustained >10% increase in product 5xx rate for >10 minutes compared to pre-roll baseline
Sustained >25ms increase in p95 latency for >10 minutes
More than 500 saga queue errors in 1h or repeated durable-store timeouts
qa_checklist: Unit tests for signature generation and header propagation
Integration tests covering deferred-saga enqueue/replay and idempotency
Chaos test: simulate durable-store partition and verify safe-fail behavior
Load test: verify canary handles 3x synthetic tenant burst without backend overload
notifications_and_followups: Notify Customers Slack channel and on-call SRE via #sre-esc for canary start/finish
Schedule postmortem window 24h after full rollout
Follow-up ticket for long-term durable store replacement (ENG-800145) if replication issues observed
